dehydrated_text:
So you may remember Roomie, the Persian poet. He also says this: the world that we live in is a prison for drunks. Okay. So, I'm pretty sure Roomie did not read Jesus' Gospel of Thomas but they're able to think the same thoughts because they're all being inspired by the same source. Does that make sense? All right.

Jesus said, "The phrases and the scribes have taken the keys of knowledge." Nostis means knowledge, okay, and hidden them. They themselves have not entered, nor have they allowed others to enter those who wish to. You, however, be as wise as serpents and as innocent as children.

Okay, so Jesus hates organized religion. The Pharisees are Jewish priests and leaders who create a hierarchy of religion where they say only they know the truth and that you must listen to them. Jesus says they themselves are ignorant because you cannot access knowledge through hierarchy or by oppressing others; you can only gain it by looking within yourself. You have to become like the serpent, pretending not to know anything, in order to access this knowledge yourself, because otherwise, if you're capable of accessing knowledge, the priest will see you as a threat and kill you.

And remember, what the serpent did to Eve was to tell her to eat from the fruit. So Jesus is saying it is good and natural to seek knowledge even if it means disobeying God. That's what we're meant to do here: seek knowledge, truth, love. If the gods or priests stop you from doing so, it's because they are evil.

The true God, the monad, is pure love, compassion, and forgiveness. He can do no wrong and is perfection. If you have the desire to seek knowledge and believe that knowledge makes you a happier, more fulfilled person, then you should seek it. Even if God tells you not to, because if that god tells you not to, he's a false god.

Jesus said, "Whoever has come to understand the world as found only a corpse, and whoever has found a corpse is superior to the world." This is what will get Jesus in trouble, right? He’s saying the Roman Empire, this great empire that ranges across the Mediterranean, it’s a corpse. It's dying. It's dead. It's nothing. Once you recognize this and refuse to comply or obey, they have no power over you.

The kingdom is like a shepherd who had 100 sheep. One of them, the largest, went astray. He left the 99 and looked for that one until he found it. When he had gone to such trouble, he said to the sheep, "I care for you more than the 99." God, the true God, does not want obedience; he wants us to be creative, seek knowledge, discover, explore, try new things. And if we do this, he cares for us more than those who obey him.

When we love and imagine, we make the universe a brighter place. We are shining our light. When we sit back and just do what we're told, we're doing nothing. We’re like NPCs—non-playable characters in video games. We don't exist. Jesus said, "A man had received visitors, and when he had prepared the dinner, he sent his servant to invite the guests." He went to the first one and said, “My master invites you.” The guest replied, “I have claimed again some merchants; they are coming to me this evening. I must go and give them my orders. I asked to be excused from the dinner.”

He went to another and said, "My master has invited you." The guest said, "I have just bought a house and am required for the day. I shall not have any spare time."

He went to another and said, "My master invites you." The guest replied, "My friends are getting married and I am to prepare the banquet. I shall not be able to come. I ask to be excused from the dinner.”

He went to another and said, "My master advised you." The guest said, "I have just bought a farm and I'm on my way to collect the rent.”
